'''Igor Dvornik''' (9 May 1923, [[Split, Croatia|Split]] – 21 August 2010, [[Zagreb]]) was a [[Croatia]]n [[radiation chemistry|radiation chemist]].

Dvornik proposed and developed two original chemical [[dosimetry]] systems based on [[ethanol]]-[[chlorobenzene]] solutions of which the one designed for high-doses is accepted as an [[International Organization for Standardization|ISO]] standard and is one of the most widely used dosimetry systems. His work in understanding high [[hydrochloric acid]] yield of the ethanol-chlorobenzene dosimeter led to him being among the first to propose the existence of presolvated 'dry' electron reactions.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Dvornik, I |author2=Zec, U |author3=Ranogajec, F | title=The Ethanol-Chlorobenzene Aerated System as a New High-Level Dosimeter for Routine Measurements | publisher=Food Irradiation. Proceedings of the International Symposium on Food Irradiation | year=1966}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |author1=A Vértes |author2=S Nagy |author3=Z Klencsár |author4=RG Lovas |author5=F Rösch | title=Handbook of Nuclear Chemistry | publisher=Springer | year=2011 | isbn=978-1-4419-0719-6}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title=In memoriam: Igor Dvornik | journal=Radiation Physics and Chemistry | year=2012 | volume=81 | issue=9 | pages=1283–1284 | doi=10.1016/j.radphyschem.2012.06.008| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title=Dr. Igor Dvornik (1923–2010) | journal=Periodicum Biologorum | year=2010 | volume=112 | number=4 | pages=493–496 | url=http://hrcak.srce.hr/63698}}</ref><ref>[http://www.irb.hr/eng/News/Croatian-Dosimetry-System-among-Best-in-the-World irb.hr] | retrieved March 24, 2015.</ref>
